title: Tour Guides and Escorts
description: Escort individuals or groups on sightseeing tours or through places of interest, such as industrial establishments, public buildings, and art galleries.

tasks.text: Describe tour points of interest to group members, and respond to questions.
Escort individuals or groups on cruises, sightseeing tours, or through places of interest, such as industrial establishments, public buildings, or art galleries.
Monitor visitors' activities to ensure compliance with establishment or tour regulations and safety practices.
Conduct educational activities for school children.
Research various topics, including site history, environmental conditions, and clients' skills and abilities to plan appropriate expeditions, instruction, and commentary.
Provide directions and other pertinent information to visitors.
Select travel routes and sites to be visited based on knowledge of specific areas.
Provide for physical safety of groups, performing such activities as providing first aid or directing emergency evacuations.
Assemble and check the required supplies and equipment prior to departure.
Greet and register visitors, and issue any required identification badges or safety devices.
Distribute brochures, show audiovisual presentations, and explain establishment processes and operations at tour sites.
Drive motor vehicles to transport visitors to establishments and tour site locations.
Provide information about wildlife varieties and habitats, as well as any relevant regulations, such as those pertaining to hunting and fishing.
Teach skills, such as proper climbing methods, and demonstrate and advise on the use of equipment.
Collect fees and tickets from group members.
Perform clerical duties, such as filing, typing, operating switchboards, or routing mail and messages.
Solicit tour patronage and sell souvenirs.
Speak foreign languages to communicate with foreign visitors.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Photoshop, SmugMug Flickr.

skills.name: Internet browser software
skills.def: Software to view the contents of web pages and to navigate from one page to another. Examples: Apple Safari, Microsoft Internet Explorer.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint, Pear Deck.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Facebook.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Microsoft Access.
